articles.title: The Minimum IAM Policy for an S3 Web Client: One Bucket, Least Privilege
articles.excerpt: The quickest policies to give a web file manager’s access key are the broad ones. AWS’s managed AdministratorAccess policy allows "Action" : "*" on "Resource" : "*", and AmazonS3FullAccess allows s3:*…
articles.body: The quickest policies to give a web file manager’s access key are the broad ones. AWS’s managed AdministratorAccess policy allows "Action" : "*" on "Resource" : "*" , and AmazonS3FullAccess allows s3:* on every resource, so either key works on every bucket in the account. AWS’s IAM guidance is to “grant only the permissions required to perform a task” , and it warns that AWS managed policies “might not grant least-privilege permissions” for your use. It prefers temporary credentials, but names third-party clients that don’t support IAM Identity Center as the case for an IAM user’s long-term access keys, which is where a web client sits.

articles.title: What Is IDOR? Insecure Direct Object Reference Explained with Real Examples
articles.excerpt: IDOR is one of the most common security bugs we find when testing web applications and APIs. It is simple to understand, often easy to exploit, and it can expose the private data of every user on a pl…
articles.body: IDOR is one of the most common security bugs we find when testing web applications and APIs. It is simple to understand, often easy to exploit, and it can expose the private data of every user on a platform. In this guide we explain what an IDOR vulnerability is, how attackers find it, real examples, and how developers can fix it for good. What is IDOR? IDOR stands for Insecure Direct Object Reference. It happens when an application uses an ID that the user can change (such as an invoice number, user ID or file name) to fetch data, but never checks whether that user is actually allowed to see or change that data. Think of a hotel where every room key opens any door, as long as you know the room number. You only booked room 101, but nothing stops you from walking into room 102.
articles.author: Bugfynd

articles.title: AgentTaint: a provenance firewall for MCP tool calls
articles.excerpt: Agents that can call tools do not only generate text. They send email, write files, open URLs, and run commands. A lot of that is triggered after the model has read something untrusted: a web page, an…
articles.body: Agents that can call tools do not only generate text. They send email, write files, open URLs, and run commands. A lot of that is triggered after the model has read something untrusted: a web page, an email, a document. Filtering the prompt for suspicious phrases is a weak control once the dangerous part is a destination hidden in content the agent just ingested. AgentTaint is a provenance-aware firewall for Model Context Protocol tool calls. It sits between an MCP client and the real MCP server and returns ALLOW , CONFIRM , or BLOCK for each tools/call , based on where sensitive arguments came from. I am Marouane El Aasri, a software developer. The project is a research release under the Apache License 2.0. What it is not It is not a prompt-injection classifier.

articles.title: Cosmic 'betta fish' glows in spectacular nebula portrait | Space photo of the day for Nov. 26, 2026
articles.excerpt: The striking blue of the Betta Fish Nebula swims across the cosmic landscape in a new image from the Dark Energy Camera.
articles.body: An image captured by the Dark Energy Camera showcasing the Betta Fish Nebula. (Image credit: CTIO/NOIRLab/DOE/NSF/AURA) The striking blue of the Betta Fish Nebula swims across the cosmic landscape, a stunning wisp of material leftover from a stellar explosion. What is it? Roughly 6,800 light-years from Earth and nestled in the Centaurus constellation, this piece of the supernova remnant SNR G295.5+09.7 has earned the nickname the Betta Fish Nebula for its floaty, fishy shape. This almost ghostly whirl of gas and dust was created when a star much more massive than our sun exploded, blasting its outer layers of material outward in the process. Over time, the remnants of this supernova eruption stretched outward into space, dispersing and colliding with surrounding gas.
